proposal.hypothesis: The pudding box is pinched near its top edge with little pad area, and the fast lift adds inertial load, so it slips out during the hold. A deeper, slower grasp keeps more contact area and less dynamic load.
proposal.rationale: rtr001_pudding_box reached travel_reached=0.04567 against travel_required=0.03. So the box was lifted and then lost: felt.stopped_by=slip, pad_drop_t=3.02, and payload_held_g is empty. That is a hold failure, not an approach failure. peak_force=26.69 N is the lowest of the three, and its surprise_z travel_reached=-1.353 says it lifted less than expected. A deeper grasp gives more pad contact on the 38.5 mm-tall box. A slower close and lift lowers the inertial load (peak_wrist_acc=2.914 m/s2) on the 187 g box while the jaws hold it.

proposal.hypothesis: The wide objects fail on aperture and face splay. At 25° the faces are only parallel at a moderate opening, and the 2 mm TPU plus the 3 mm groove use up opening width, so 57–90 mm objects are hit by the jaw edge and squeezed out.
proposal.rationale: Each object is wider than the measured widest grip on these fingers. gelatin_box width_mm=73 and pudding_box width_mm=89.6 are both over box=65, and cup width_mm=57 is over cylinder=50. contact_types=edge,pinch on all three shows a jaw edge landing on the object instead of a clean pinch. That matches the high peak_force (45.51, 26.69, 74.82 N) and the cup being knocked away (travel_reached=1.63, payload_held_g=0.6). it001 changed the pads more broadly (tilt, TPU and width together) and caused 2 regressions. This proposal leaves width_mm alone and changes three parameters. Each stays inside the allowed relative change. Tilting the pads further makes the faces parallel at a wider opening. A thinner TPU skin (still 0.9 friction) and a shallower groove give back aperture on each jaw.
ruled_out: rung0: widest grip (box=65, cylinder=50 mm) is below width_mm 73 and 57, and no grasp parameter widens the jaw opening
rung1: every recomposition still uses the same grasp motor, and contact_types=edge shows the jaws cannot get around the object at all
rung2: the rack is empty, so there is no existing tool to use or adapt
rung3: the tool templates (pad, hook, knob_cup, soft_tip, slot_inserter, probe) give single-point contacts, but these objects accept only pinch, which needs both jaws

proposal.hypothesis: At 7.4 V the gripper's stall torque gives too little normal force to hold heavier boxes against gravity and lift acceleration, so they slip during the hold.
proposal.rationale: All three failures end with felt.stopped_by=slip and a pad pressure drop (pad_drop_t 3.14, 3.02, 4.22 s). The gripper runs at 7.4 V. The 187 g pudding box lifted past travel (0.04567 > 0.03) and then slipped, so squeeze force is too low even though the TPU friction is 0.9. Moving only the gripper servo to 12 V raises its stall torque and so the squeeze when the servo stalls on the object. The other joints stay as they are, which keeps the risk of regressions low.
ruled_out: rung0: grasp has no grip-force parameter, because the squeeze is set by where the servo stalls, and slip continued across the depth and speed ranges System 1 already searched (s1_exhausted)
rung1: no composition of existing primitives raises jaw normal force
rung2: the rack is empty, so there is no tool to use
rung3: tool templates do not add pinch squeeze for the stock jaws
rung4: the fingers already have a 0.9-friction TPU skin, and it001's finger change still regressed, so finger geometry alone does not fix the low squeeze on heavier objects
